slot.subtopic: Stability of alkenes / heat of hydrogenation
slot.brief: Rank four simple alkenes (varying substitution) in order of stability; expect justification via hyperconjugation and heat of hydrogenation.

stem: Which sequence gives the alkenes in decreasing order of stability?

verdicts.working: Alkene stability generally increases with the number of alkyl groups attached to the C=C: 2-methyl-2-butene (trisubstituted) > 2-methylpropene (disubstituted) > propene (monosubstituted) > ethene (unsubstituted).

working:
Alkene stability increases with the number of alkyl substituents on the double bond (greater hyperconjugative stabilisation).\nTri-substituted $>$ di-substituted $>$ mono-substituted $>$ unsubstituted.\nHeat of hydrogenation magnitude follows the reverse order.

Independent check: Alkene stability generally increases with the number of alkyl groups attached to the C=C: 2-methyl-2-butene (trisubstituted) > 2-methylpropene (disubstituted) > propene (monosubstituted) > ethene (unsubstituted).
solution:
Alkene stability increases with the number of alkyl groups attached to the double bond due to greater hyperconjugative stabilisation:
$$\text{trisubstituted} > \text{disubstituted} > \text{monosubstituted} > \text{unsubstituted}$$
Hence, $\text{2-methyl-2-butene} > \text{2-methylpropene} > \text{propene} > \text{ethene}$.
